newsitem.title: PERU: Whole of Lima placed under emergency rule.
newsitem.headline: Whole of Lima placed under emergency rule.

text.p: Peru's government placed the whole of Lima and the neighbouring port of Callao under a state of emergency on Friday in response to the seizure of hostages at the Japanese ambassador's residence.

Under a decree published in the official government gazette and signed by President Alberto Fujimori, emergency rule was extended for 60 days to allow the government to take "corrective action" against subversion.
Previously, only the centre and industrialised outskirts of the Peruvian capital were under a state of emergency.
Emergency rule, which gives the government greater powers in combatting leftist rebels, puts areas under armed forces' control and suspends many constitutional rights.
Despite a dramatic drop in rebel attacks since the height of the guerrilla conflict between the mid-1980s and the early 1990s, emergency rule continues in about 30 percent of Peru.
